standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that zero cycles are generated by classes of closed points with separable residue fields
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows writing a multiple of the difference of the two points as a combination of classes of points with separable residue fields.

standard_prerequisites.name: Poincare duality for zero dimensional schemes and the trace description of the degree map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the computation of the cohomology of a zero dimensional scheme, including the identification of the degree map with the trace, and axiom (A)(b) expressing the pairing as pullbacks followed by traces
standard_prerequisites.use: Dualizes the cohomological relation into a relation between trace maps out of the degree zero cohomology.

standard_prerequisites.name: A relation between traces of surjective algebra maps forces equality
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the algebraic lemma stating that a relation between traces of surjective maps of finite separable algebras forces the two surjections to agree
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the two pullback maps along the points coincide, contradicting the assumption on the cycle classes.

core_obligations: Set up the contradiction (proof lines 3659-3667): the case of distinct irreducible components is immediate, so the scheme may be assumed irreducible; assuming the difference of the two points is divisible by an integer larger than one, write the quotient as a combination of classes of points with separable residue fields.

Dualize the relation (proof lines 3667-3682): applying the cycle class map gives a cohomological relation among the classes of the points involved; by Poincare duality in the form of the pairing axiom this relation is dual to an identity between the traces of the pullback maps to the cohomologies of those points, viewed as maps from the degree zero cohomology of the scheme to the coefficient field.

Contradict the assumption (proof lines 3682-3694): the pullback maps along the two rational points are surjective and their composites with the comparison map from the degree zero cohomology of the base are isomorphisms, so the algebraic relation between traces applies and shows that the two pullback maps agree; this contradicts the assumption that the cycle classes of the two points differ.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an irreducible scheme and write the divisible difference in terms of points.
Dualize the cohomological relation into an identity of traces.
Apply the algebraic trace relation to force equality of the pullbacks, contradicting the assumption.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if the cycle classes of two rational points of a smooth projective scheme differ, then their difference is not divisible by any integer larger than one in the group of zero cycles (statement lines 3655-3663). The proof (proof lines 3664-3694) writes a supposed divisibility in terms of points with separable residue fields, dualizes the resulting cohomological relation into an identity between traces, and applies the algebraic trace relation to derive a contradiction. H3: a duality argument with an algebraic relation, written out in full.
